mainTopic: When טומאה cancels a נזיר's earlier days (refuting עולא's reading of רבי אליעזר, and the minimum 'days'). Also a new משנה on a נזיר who finished outside ארץ ישראל.
overview: רבא gives a פסוק as the source for רבי אליעזר's view as עולא understood it. He reads 'כי טמא נזרו' as speaking about someone who vowed נזירות while already טמא. אביי refutes this with a ברייתא that applies 'והימים הראשונים יפלו' to a נזיר who was טהור when he vowed and only became impure later. The ברייתא gives three cases: impure on the first day, on day 100, and on day 99, and only the last case cancels his days. רב פפא then asks how many days count as 'days', and רבא answers from the word 'יפלו'. The גמרא explains that the words 'ימים' and 'יפלו' together set the minimum at one full day plus the start of a second. A new משנה follows about a נזיר who finished his term outside ארץ ישראל: בית שמאי require 30 more days, and בית הלל require the whole term again. The משנה tells the story of הילני המלכה, who ended up keeping 21 years, though רבי יהודה says only 14. The גמרא begins to suggest that the argument depends on whether the טומאה of ארץ העמים was decreed only on its earth, and this discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבא gives the reason for רבי אליעזר's view
steps.stepSummary: רבא says רבי אליעזר's ruling comes from the words 'כי טמא נזרו', meaning the person vowed נזירות while already impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: What is רבי אליעזר's reason? The verse says 'because his נזירות was impure', meaning he made his vow of נזירות while he was impure.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains the source for רבי אליעזר's opinion, following the way עולא understood it. He reads the פסוק as talking about someone who was already טמא when he became a נזיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'כי טמא נזרו' literally mean 'for his נזירות was impure.' רבא takes this to mean the נזירות itself began in a state of טומאה. If that reading is right, the rule in this פסוק would apply only to a טמא שנזר, a person who vowed while impure.

keyTerms.meaning: 'For his נזירות was impure' (a phrase from the פסוק)

phrases.english: Rava said:
What is the reason of Rabbi Eliezer?
The verse says: "because his nezirus was impure" —
because he vowed nezirus while in impurity.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies a פסוק as the source for עולא's understanding of רבי אליעזר, which was discussed earlier on the דף.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר's ruling is based on 'כי טמא נזרו', read as describing someone who vowed נזירות while impure.

steps.title: אביי objects from a ברייתא: impure at the start of 100 days
steps.stepSummary: אביי quotes a ברייתא. A נזיר for 100 days who becomes טמא right at the start loses nothing, because he has no 'first days' to lose yet.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי objected: Someone said 'I am a נזיר for 100 days' and became impure at the beginning of the 100. You might think this cancels his days. The verse teaches 'and the first days shall fall away', which means only once he has first days, and this person has no first days.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי begins an objection to רבא by quoting a ברייתא that reads the words 'והימים הראשונים יפלו' closely. This is the first of three cases, and the point of the objection will be spelled out in step 5.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says that losing days requires having some 'first days' already counted. Here the person vowed first and became טמא only afterward, at the very start, so he lost nothing. This shows the ברייתא is applying the פסוק to someone who was טהור when he vowed.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised an objection to him (from an earlier source)
I am hereby a נזיר (the words of the vow)
Cancels the days already counted, so they must be counted again
'And the first days shall fall away' (a phrase from the פסוק)

phrases.english: Abaye objected to him:
"I am hereby a nazir for one hundred days,"
and he became impure at the beginning of the hundred,
one might think it should cancel [his days],
so the verse teaches: "And the first days shall fall away" —
only once he has first days,
and this one has no first days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a challenge to רבא's explanation in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's (and עולא's) claim that the rule of 'first days falling away' applies only to someone who vowed while impure.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא applies the words 'והימים הראשונים יפלו' to a person who vowed and only afterward became impure, so the פסוק is not limited to a טמא שנזר.

steps.title: The ברייתא continues: impure on day 100
steps.stepSummary: If he becomes טמא at the end of the 100 days, he loses nothing, because 'first days' implies there must also be 'last days' still to come.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he became impure at the end of the hundred, you might think it cancels his days. The verse teaches 'and the first days shall fall away', which implies there are also last days, and this person has no last days.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא that אביי is quoting moves to a second case: becoming טמא on the very last day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Calling some days 'first' implies there are other days that count as 'last.' On day 100 his נזירות term is already complete, so nothing is left to count as 'last days.' The earlier days therefore do not fall away.

keyTerms.meaning: At the end of the hundred (on day 100)

phrases.english: If he became impure at the end of the hundred,
one might think it should cancel [his days],
so the verse teaches: "And the first days shall fall away" —
which implies there are also last days,
and this one has no last days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא quoted in step 2 with a second case.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's reading of the פסוק: 'first' implies 'last'.

steps.title: The ברייתא continues: impure on day 99
steps.stepSummary: If he becomes טמא on day 99, his days are cancelled, because he has both 'first days' behind him and 'last days' still ahead.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he became impure on day 100 minus one, you might think it does not cancel his days. The verse teaches 'and the first days shall fall away', which implies there are also last days, and this person has both first and last days.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes with a third case: becoming טמא one day before the end. Here the days do fall away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On day 99 he already has earlier days counted and still has a day left. Both conditions of the פסוק are met, so he loses his earlier days. Together with the first two cases, this gives a full picture of when the פסוק's rule applies.

phrases.english: If he became impure on day one hundred minus one,
one might think it should not cancel [his days],
so the verse teaches: "And the first days shall fall away" —
which implies there are also last days,
and this one has both first and last days.

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's three cases: impure at the start means no loss (no first days), impure on day 100 means no loss (no last days), and impure on day 99 means the days are lost (both first and last days).
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא with its third case.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's reading of the פסוק: losing days requires both first and last days.

steps.title: The ברייתא cannot be about someone who vowed while impure, so it is a refutation
steps.stepSummary: אביי points out that the ברייתא describes someone who vowed and only later became טמא, yet it still applies the 'first days' rule to him. So the claim that the פסוק is limited to a טמא שנזר is refuted.
steps.simpleTranslation: But this cannot be about an impure person who made a vow. It teaches 'I am a נזיר for a hundred' and then 'he became impure at the beginning of the hundred', and it also teaches 'only once he has first days.' This is a refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי spells out the point of his objection, and the גמרא declares a תיובתא, meaning the explanation from step 1 is defeated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'ונטמא בתחלת מאה' show the person became impure after his vow, so he was טהור when he vowed. Even so, the ברייתא uses the 'first days' reading of the פסוק to decide his case. That shows the פסוק is not limited to a טמא שנזר, which knocks out the reading that רבא gave following עולא.

keyTerms.meaning: An impure person who vowed נזירות

phrases.english: But this — about an impure person who vowed —
you cannot say [it is speaking],
since it teaches "I am hereby a nazir for a hundred,"
and he became impure at the beginning of the hundred,
and it teaches "only once he has first days,"
This is a refutation.

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא applies 'והימים הראשונים יפלו' to a נזיר who was טהור when he vowed. So the reading that limits the פסוק to a טמא שנזר is refuted.
steps.confusionAlert: The first case in the ברייתא ends with 'no loss', but that does not help רבא. The point is that the ברייתא is analyzing a person who was טהור when he vowed by using this פסוק at all, which proves the פסוק covers such a person.
steps.whyThisMatters: A תיובתא means the explanation is rejected. The rule of losing earlier days is not limited to someone who vowed while impure.
steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא, בְּטָמֵא שֶׁנָּזַר לָא מָצֵית אָמְרַתְּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the ברייתא in steps 2 through 4 against step 1.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: עולא's reading of רבי אליעזר, with רבא's source for it, is refuted, because the ברייתא applies the פסוק to someone who became impure after his vow.

steps.title: How many days count as 'days'?
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks אביי what the minimum is for the 'first days' that טומאה cancels. Is it one day finished and the second begun, or two days finished and the third begun?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to אביי: These 'days' we keep talking about, does it mean one day has passed and the second has started? Or maybe two days have passed and the third has started?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא asks a clarifying question about the 'first days' rule. He wants to know exactly how many days a נזיר must have kept before טומאה cancels them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'הימים הראשונים', and 'days' is plural. The question is whether a plural needs only one full day plus part of a second, or two full days plus part of a third. The answer decides at what point the טומאה starts to cancel his count.

keyTerms.meaning: Days, in the plural, from the פסוק 'הַיָּמִים הָרִאשֹׁנִים'
Went out, meaning a day that has finished
Begin, meaning a day that has started
Or perhaps, which introduces the second option

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Abaye:
Those 'days' that we have been talking about,
phrases.notes: These are the 'first days' from the earlier steps, the ones that get cancelled when the נזיר becomes טמא.

phrases.english: does it mean one day has finished and a second has started,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִּלְמָא דְּנָפְקִין תְּרֵין וּמַתְחִילִין תְּלָתָא?
phrases.english: or perhaps two have finished and a third has started?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב פָּפָּא לְאַבָּיֵי: הָלֵין יָמִים דְּקָאָמְרִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the 'first days' idea was established in the ברייתא, רב פפא asks for its exact measurement.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The minimum number of days the word 'days' requires: one day finished with the second begun, or two days finished with the third begun.

steps.title: רבא answers from the word יפלו
steps.stepSummary: אביי has no answer, so רב פפא asks רבא. רבא answers that the word 'יפלו' is written in the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי did not have an answer. רב פפא went and asked רבא, who told him: It says 'יפלו'.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי cannot answer, so רב פפא brings the question to רבא. רבא answers by pointing to the word יפלו in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's short answer is that one finished day plus part of a second day is enough. The next step explains how the word יפלו shows this.

keyTerms.meaning: He did not have it in hand, meaning he had no answer
They shall fall away, meaning the days are cancelled

phrases.english: He did not have the answer,
so he came and asked Rava.
He said to him: It is written 'shall be void.'

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא הֲוָה בִּידֵיהּ, אֲתָא שַׁיְילֵיהּ לְרָבָא
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Because the פסוק writes 'יפלו', one day finished and the second begun is enough.

steps.title: Why the תורה needed both 'ימים' and 'יפלו'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that each word teaches something. Without יפלו, we would think two full days are needed. Without ימים, we would think even one day is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both words had to be written. If the תורה wrote only 'ימים', I would think we need two days finished and a third begun, so it wrote 'יפלו'. If it wrote only 'יפלו', I would think even one day is enough, so it wrote 'ימים'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the פסוק needed both words. It shows that each word blocks a different wrong conclusion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word pulls the measurement in a different direction. 'ימים' alone would push the minimum up to two full days, and 'יפלו' brings it down. 'יפלו' alone would let it drop to a single day, and 'ימים' keeps it at more than one. Together they set the rule: one full day plus the start of a second.

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One, meaning the תורה
I would have said, meaning the mistaken first thought
Enter, meaning a day that has begun

steps.whatToRemember: The 'first days' are cancelled once one day has finished and the second has begun. Both words in the פסוק are needed to set this.

phrases.english: It was necessary to write 'days'
and it was necessary to write 'shall be void,'
for if the Merciful One had written 'days'
and had not written 'shall be void,'

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה אָמֵינָא: עַד דְּנָפְקִין תְּרֵין וְעָיְילִין תְּלָתָא,
phrases.english: I would have said: not until two have finished and a third has begun,
so the Merciful One wrote 'shall be void.'
And if it had written 'shall be void' and not written 'days,'
I would have said even one day is enough,
so the Merciful One wrote 'days.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains רבא's answer and why both words in the פסוק are needed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'first days' rule needs one full day plus the start of a second. 'ימים' and 'יפלו' each set one side of this limit.

steps.title: A נזיר who finished outside ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה. Someone finished a long נזירות outside ארץ ישראל and then came to ארץ ישראל. בית שמאי say he keeps 30 more days. בית הלל say he starts his whole נזירות over.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone vowed a long נזירות, finished it, and then came to ארץ ישראל. בית שמאי say he must be a נזיר for 30 more days. בית הלל say he must be a נזיר from the beginning again.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It presents a מחלוקת between בית שמאי and בית הלל about a נזיר who kept his נזירות outside ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree that his נזירות outside the land is not enough, and he must keep more in ארץ ישראל. They argue about how much. בית שמאי say 30 days, which is a basic נזירות. בית הלל say the whole term he vowed.

keyTerms.meaning: From the beginning, meaning the full term again

phrases.english: MISHNA: One who vowed a long naziriteship,
phrases.notes: The case is someone who kept his נזירות outside ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: and completed his naziriteship,
and afterward came to the Land,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: נָזִיר שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם,
phrases.english: Beit Shammai say: he is a nazirite for thirty days,
and Beit Hillel say: he is a nazirite from the beginning.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי שֶׁנָּזַר נְזִירוּת הַרְבֵּה, וְהִשְׁלִים אֶת נְזִירוּתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to בית שמאי, a נזיר who finished outside the land keeps 30 more days in ארץ ישראל. According to בית הלל, he keeps his full term again.

steps.title: The story of Queen הילני
steps.stepSummary: הילני המלכה vowed seven years of נזירות if her son came back safely from war. She kept them outside the land. בית הלל told her to keep seven more in ארץ ישראל. She became טמאה at the end and kept seven more, for 21 years in total.
steps.simpleTranslation: Queen הילני's son went to war. She said: If he comes back safely, I will be a נזירה for seven years. He came back, and she was a נזירה for seven years. At the end she went up to ארץ ישראל. בית הלל ruled that she must be a נזירה for seven more years. At the end of those seven years she became טמאה. So she was a נזירה for 21 years.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה tells a real event that shows בית הלל's ruling being put into practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her first seven years outside the land were not enough, so she started over in ארץ ישראל, just as בית הלל say. Then she became טמאה at the end and lost those seven years too. That forced a third set of seven years.

phrases.english: There was an incident with Queen Helene
whose son went to war,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרָה: אִם יָבוֹא בְּנִי מִן הַמִּלְחָמָה בְּשָׁלוֹם —
phrases.english: and she said: If my son comes back from the war safely,
I will be a nazirite for seven years.
Her son came back from the war,
and she was a nazirite for seven years,
and at the end of seven years she went up to the Land,
and Beit Hillel ruled for her

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁתְּהֵא נְזִירָה עוֹד שֶׁבַע שָׁנִים אֲחֵרוֹת.
phrases.english: that she must be a nazirite for another seven years.
At the end of those seven years she became impure.
So she ended up a nazirite for twenty-one years.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows בית הלל's ruling from step 9 being followed in a real case.
steps.raayaObject: בית הלל's view that a נזיר who comes to the land starts over
steps.raayaSupportSource: The real case of הילני המלכה, where בית הלל ruled she must keep seven more years

steps.title: רבי יהודה: only fourteen years
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה disagrees with the story's total and says she was a נזירה for only 14 years.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said: She was a נזירה for only fourteen years.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה challenges how the story was told and says the total was 14 years, not 21.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה does not accept the 21-year total. The משנה does not explain here how he reaches 14; it simply records his disagreement about the count.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא הָיְתָה נְזִירָה אֶלָּא אַרְבַּע עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁנָה.
phrases.english: She was a nazirite for only fourteen years.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: לֹא הָיְתָה נְזִירָה אֶלָּא אַרְבַּע עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disputes the 21-year total given in step 10.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The total number of years in the story, not the story itself
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי יהודה holds that the count of 21 years is wrong and that it was only 14.

steps.title: The גמרא quotes the first part of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by quoting the משנה's opening argument. בית שמאי say a נזיר who arrives from outside the land keeps 30 days, and בית הלל say he starts his נזירות over.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The first part of the משנה teaches: בית שמאי say he is a נזיר for thirty days, and בית הלל say he is a נזיר from the beginning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its discussion by quoting the argument from the משנה it wants to explain. This is a setup line for the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new is ruled here. The גמרא repeats the two opinions so it can ask what idea is behind each one. 'From the beginning' means he restarts the full count of his נזירות.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
The first part of the משנה
A נזיר from the beginning, meaning he starts his whole נזירות over

phrases.english: GEMARA:
The first part teaches:

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: נָזִיר שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם,
phrases.english: Beit Shammai say: he is a nazirite for thirty days,
phrases.notes: These are 30 extra days in ארץ ישראל, on top of the נזירות he already kept outside the land (step 9).

phrases.english: and Beit Hillel say: he is a nazirite from the beginning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the story of הילני המלכה to the משנה's main argument and begins the גמרא's analysis.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי: 30 more days. בית הלל: he restarts his נזירות.

steps.title: A suggested reason: בית שמאי think only the earth was made impure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests what the argument depends on. Perhaps בית שמאי hold that the rabbis' decree of טומאה on ארץ העמים applied only to its earth.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say this is what they argue about: בית שמאי hold that the rabbis made the decree on ארץ העמים because of its earth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible explanation of the argument, using the word 'לימא' (let us say). This is only a suggestion, and the sentence goes on to give בית הלל's side next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rabbis declared lands outside ארץ ישראל טמא. Here the suggestion is that, for בית שמאי, only the soil itself was included. That is a lighter kind of טומאה, so the נזיר's earlier days still count, and he only needs 30 more days. 'לימא' usually signals an idea the גמרא may later reject.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us say (introduces a suggestion that may be rejected)
Land of the nations, meaning lands outside ארץ ישראל

steps.confusionAlert: The sentence is not finished here. בית שמאי's side is given now, and the matching reason for בית הלל continues right after.

phrases.english: Shall we say that they argue about this:
that Beit Shammai hold:

phrases.aramaic: אֶרֶץ הָעַמִּים מִשּׁוּם גּוּשָׁהּ גָּזְרוּ עָלֶיהָ,
phrases.english: the land of the nations, they decreed on it because of its earth,
phrases.notes: He means the rabbis made only the actual ground טמא, not the whole area.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After quoting the two opinions, the גמרא suggests the reason behind בית שמאי's view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Suggested: for בית שמאי, the decree on ארץ העמים covered only its earth, so the טומאה is lighter and only 30 more days are needed.
